title: Safe Storage of Medicines and Chemicals
hook: Most poisonings happen at home with everyday products. How you store them is your first line of defense.
key_points: Keep medicines and chemicals up high, out of sight, and locked when possible.
Leave products in their original, labeled containers, never food containers.
Common household poisons include medicines, cleaners, and personal care products.
Save the U.S. Poison Control number: 1-800-222-1222.
Call Poison Control right away for a suspected poisoning, even before symptoms.
content_html: Most poisonings happen at home and involve ordinary products: medicines, cleaning supplies, and personal care items. Where and how you store these is the simplest way to prevent an accident, especially with children or anyone confused around.
extra_html:
The core advice from Poison Control is to keep medicines and chemicals up high, out of sight, and locked away when you can. Just as important, keep products in their original containers with the label intact, and never transfer a chemical into a food or drink container where it could be mistaken for something safe. Store medicines separately from household cleaners.

Keep the U.S. Poison Control number handy: 1-800-222-1222, free and available around the clock. If you suspect a poisoning, call right away, even before symptoms appear. Experts can tell you whether home care is enough or whether you need emergency help, which often saves a trip to the ER and precious time.

flashcards.prompt: What is the U.S. Poison Control number, and when should you call?
flashcards.back_html: 1-800-222-1222. Call right away if you suspect a poisoning, even before symptoms appear; they can advise whether home care is enough or you need emergency help.

flashcards.prompt: Why should household chemicals stay in their original containers?

choices.text: The label identifies the product and explains what to do if it's swallowed
It makes the product last longer

flashcards.explanation_html: Original, labeled containers identify the product and carry first-aid instructions. Moving chemicals into food or drink containers is dangerous because someone may mistake them for something safe.
